purpose: Central-government MSME policy and incentive knowledge base for the Industrial Energy Transition Optimizer

policy_engine_rules.purpose: Determine whether a technically feasible industrial-energy transition pathway may qualify for central-government MSME support and calculate the applicable financial adjustment where sufficient eligibility information is available.
execution_order: Verify project type and technology eligibility
Check project cost or loan ceiling
Retrieve applicable financial support from subsidies.json where a financial support reference exists
Calculate applicable subsidy or interest support
Check whether benefits can be combined
policy_engine_rules.important_rule: A scheme being relevant to an MSME does not mean every MSME or every energy project automatically qualifies.
policy_engine_rules.verification_rule: Final eligibility must be verified against the latest scheme guidelines, implementing agency and lender requirements before a financial commitment is made.
policy_engine_rules.no_double_counting_rule: The optimizer must not automatically stack multiple subsidies for the same capital expenditure unless the respective scheme guidelines explicitly permit such convergence.
policy_engine_rules.policy_value_rule: Policy benefits must be represented separately from the underlying technology economics so that the recommendation remains auditable.
policy_engine_rules.uncertain_eligibility_rule: If eligibility cannot be established from available factory data, the optimizer must label the benefit as 'potential' rather than treating it as guaranteed.
policy_engine_rules.financial_data_ownership: Financial-support parameters such as subsidy rates, interest-subvention rates, benefit caps, loan limits and guarantee coverage must be maintained in subsidies.json as the canonical financial-support source. central_policies.json stores policy applicability, eligibility logic and references to the corresponding financial-support records.

msme_classification.basis: Investment in plant and machinery/equipment AND annual turnover
msme_classification.classification_logic: Both investment and turnover must remain within the applicable ceiling.
msme_classification.source: Ministry of MSME / Udyam Registration Portal

ADEETIE.policy_name: Assistance for Deployment of Energy Efficient Technologies in Industries and Establishments
ADEETIE.full_name: Assistance for Deployment of Energy Efficient Technologies in Industries and Establishments

optimizer_application.opex_adjustment: reduce financing-related annual cost where applicable

important_limitations: Interest subvention is not equivalent to a direct capital subsidy.
Project must satisfy scheme-specific technical and administrative requirements.
The optimizer must not assume eligibility merely because a technology saves energy.
Financial-support parameters must be retrieved from the referenced record in subsidies.json.
ADEETIE.source: Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Government of India

MSE_GIFT.policy_name: MSE Green Investment and Financing for Transformation
MSE_GIFT.administering_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
important_limitations: MSE-GIFT is for Micro and Small Enterprises, not automatically Medium Enterprises.
Eligible project categories and lending conditions must be satisfied.
Interest subvention must not be confused with a reduction in project CAPEX.
Financial-support parameters must be retrieved from the referenced record in subsidies.json.

MSE_SPICE.policy_name: Scheme for Promotion and Investment in Circular Economy
MSE_SPICE.administering_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
important_limitations: Only eligible brownfield projects should be considered.
The subsidy applies to eligible plant and machinery according to scheme rules, not automatically to the entire project cost.
The applicable subsidy rate and maximum subsidy must be retrieved from the referenced record in subsidies.json.
Do not apply SPICE merely because a project reduces CO2.

ZED.policy_name: MSME Sustainable Zero Defect Zero Effect Certification
ZED.administering_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
ZED.objective: Promote manufacturing with high quality and productivity while minimizing environmental impact through cleaner and more efficient processes.

optimizer_application.use_case: reduce eligible technology certification, handholding or cleaner-technology expenditure where applicable

important_limitations: ZED is primarily a certification and competitiveness programme, not a general renewable-energy subsidy.
Do not subtract the full ZED benefit from every energy-transition CAPEX calculation.
Only apply technology-upgradation support where the project satisfies the relevant ZED component.
Financial-support parameters must be retrieved from the referenced record in subsidies.json.

MSME_LEAN.administering_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
MSME_LEAN.objective: Improve MSME productivity, efficiency and competitiveness through reduction of process waste, inventory waste, space waste and energy consumption.

optimizer_application.use_case: identify process-efficiency interventions that reduce energy demand before technology replacement

MSME_LEAN.architecture_role: The optimizer should treat Lean-type efficiency measures as demand-reduction interventions that can be evaluated before generation or fuel-switching investments.

CGTMSE.policy_name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises
CGTMSE.administering_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
CGTMSE.implementing_agency: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises
CGTMSE.policy_objective: Increase availability of institutional credit to MSEs without requiring conventional collateral or third-party guarantees.

optimizer_application.financing_adjustment: reduce collateral/credit-risk barrier rather than directly reducing technology CAPEX
optimizer_application.use_case: identify pathways that can be financed through eligible collateral-free credit

CGTMSE.important_limitation: CGTMSE is a credit guarantee to the lender, not a cash subsidy paid directly to the MSME.

PMEGP.administering_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

optimizer_application.use_case: consider only when the optimizer is modelling establishment of a new eligible micro enterprise

important_limitations: Do not apply PMEGP to every existing industrial energy-retrofit project.
PMEGP is primarily for setting up new micro enterprises.
Existing units that have already received government subsidy under specified schemes may be ineligible.
Project cost limits, beneficiary contribution and margin-money subsidy parameters must be retrieved from the referenced record in subsidies.json.

RAMP.administering_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

optimizer_application.use_case: identify relevant RAMP-linked sub-schemes and programmes rather than applying one universal RAMP subsidy
optimizer_application.important_rule: RAMP is an umbrella programme; its individual interventions have separate eligibility and benefit rules.

MSE_CDP.policy_name: Micro and Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme
MSE_CDP.administering_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
MSE_CDP.objective: Improve productivity and competitiveness of MSE clusters through common facilities, infrastructure and cluster-level interventions.
special_category_conditions: clusters with more than 50 percent women-owned units
clusters with more than 50 percent micro/village units
clusters with more than 50 percent SC/ST-owned units
MSE_CDP.important_limitation: MSE-CDP is primarily a cluster-level mechanism and should not be treated as an automatic individual-factory CAPEX subsidy. Financial-support parameters must be retrieved from the referenced record in subsidies.json.

MSME_CHAMPIONS.administering_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
MSME_CHAMPIONS.objective: Improve MSME competitiveness through quality, sustainability, productivity, innovation, technology and digital adoption.

optimizer_application.use_case: support the non-energy financial and capability dimensions of transition projects

PUBLIC_PROCUREMENT_POLICY.policy_name: Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises
PUBLIC_PROCUREMENT_POLICY.administering_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
market_support_features: tender fee exemption subject to applicable rules
earnest money deposit exemption subject to applicable rules
purchase preference mechanisms subject to applicable rules

optimizer_application.use_case: potentially quantify additional market-access value for an MSME that manufactures eligible clean-energy or energy-efficient equipment/services
optimizer_application.financial_modeling: do not assign a generic monetary subsidy

TECHNOLOGY_CENTRES.policy_name: MSME Tool Rooms and Technology Centres
TECHNOLOGY_CENTRES.administering_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

optimizer_application.use_case: identify access to government technology centres for technology validation, testing, process improvement and workforce training

electrification.note: Eligibility depends on whether the specific equipment and project satisfy the applicable scheme.

solar_pv.note: This file does not assume a universal central MSME solar capital subsidy.

biomass.note: Biomass eligibility should be evaluated against the actual project and scheme definitions rather than assuming every biomass boiler receives a subsidy.

credit_guarantee.treatment: credit guarantee reduces lender credit risk; it is not a direct cash subsidy

anti_error_rules: Do not apply MSE-GIFT to Medium Enterprises.
Do not apply MSE-SPICE to projects that are not eligible brownfield projects.
Do not apply PMEGP to an ordinary existing-factory retrofit without checking PMEGP's new-enterprise conditions.
Do not treat ADEETIE interest subvention as a capital subsidy.
Do not treat CGTMSE guarantee coverage as money received by the factory.
Do not treat RAMP's total outlay as a subsidy available directly to an individual MSME.
Do not treat MSE-CDP cluster grants as individual-factory grants.
Do not assume ZED certification support pays for the entire energy-transition project.
Do not double-count benefits from multiple central schemes without checking convergence rules.
Do not use old MSME classification thresholds.
Do not treat a scheme as guaranteed merely because the factory is Udyam registered.
Do not calculate policy benefits before technical feasibility is established.
Do not allow policy incentives to make an otherwise technically infeasible pathway feasible.
Do not hide policy assumptions inside CAPEX; preserve gross CAPEX, policy benefit and net CAPEX separately.
Do not duplicate financial-support parameters from subsidies.json inside this policy file.
When a policy contains a financial_support_reference, retrieve the corresponding financial parameters from subsidies.json.
